Neutral Citation No. - 2023:Ahc:146345
Court No. - 73
Case :- Criminal Misc Anticipatory Bail Application U/S 438 Cr.P.C. No. - 9243 of 2022

Applicant :- Anurag Mishra
Opposite Party :- State of U.P.

Counsel for Applicant :- Ritukar Gupta,Deeksha Gupta,Sr. Advocate
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.,Mohammad Alam,Parvesh Kumar Pandey
Hon'ble Nalin Kumar Srivastava,J.

1. Heard learned counsel for the applicant, learned Aga and perused the material available on
record.

2. This application for anticipatory bail has been filed by applicant- Anurag Mishra in connection
with Case Crime No. 417 of 2018, under sections 419, 420, 498-A, 376, 506 Ipc, P.S. Shahganj,
District Allahabad.

3.  It is alleged in the F.I.R. that the marriage of the prosecutrix was scheduled to be held on 06.05.2018 with the present applicant but on 11.03.2018, when she went to the applicant on his call,
he forcefully made physical relation with her in a hotel and also obtained a video thereof.
Subsequently, on demand of heavy dowry, the marriage was postponed but under pressure of police on 11.07.2018, marriage within the two took place in the court before a notary and application for court marriage was also moved but no subsequent steps were taken by the accused persons including the present applicant but subsequently, proper marriage was refused by all the accused persons.

F.I.R. was lodged on 21.09.2018 and investigation started and now charge sheet has been Anurag Mishra vs State Of U.P. on 21 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/151251600/
1 submitted.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 4. It has been argued by the learned counsel for the applicant that applicant is innocent and he has apprehension of arrest in the above-mentioned case, whereas there is no credible evidence against him.
Allegations levelled against the applicant are false.
Charge sheet in the matter has been submitted.
In case applicant is granted anticipatory bail, he shall not misuse the liberty of bail and would obey all conditions of bail.

5. It is further submitted that as per F.I.R, the prosecutrix is the wife of the applicant and that is why, allegations relating to an offence under Section 498-A I.P.C. have been levelled in the F.I.R.
and if it is so, no allegation of rape can be levelled against the applicant.
It is next submitted that in her statement under Section 164 Cr.P.C., the prosecutrix has admitted that she is the wife of the applicant.

It is next submitted that the Gram Pradhan of the village also issued a certificate to this effect that the marriage between the prosecutrix and applicant has taken place on 03.10.2017 and after marriage, the prosecutrix had been residing with the applicant in her matrimonial home.
It is further submitted that even in the family register, the name of the prosecutrix is shown as the wife of the applicant in 2017 itself.
It is also submitted that the said document was corroborated by Gram Panchayat, Secretary in his statement given to the I.O. under Section 161 Cr.P.C.

It is next submitted that earlier, an Application U/s 482 Cr.P.C. No.21674 of 2019 was moved by the applicant, which was disposed of by the coordinate Bench of this Court vide order dated 08.08.2019 with the direction to the applicant to appear and surrender before the court below within 30 days and apply for bail.

It is next submitted that the applicant did not appear before the court concerned and another Application U/s 482 Cr.P.C. No.35498 of 2019 was moved but no interim protection granted to the applicant.
It is next submitted that the informant side falsely implicated the applicant and his family members in Case Crime No.207 of 2019, under Sections 419, 420, 406, 506, 120-B I.P.C.

However, Anticipatory Bail Application No.8132 of 2022 was moved by the applicant which was allowed by the coordinate Bench of this Court vide order dated 13.10.2022 and the applicant was granted anticipatory bail till conclusion of trial.
It is next submitted that in the further investigation of the case, the Investigating Officer had given a conclusion in Parcha No.5 that no case is made out against the present applicant.

It is next submitted that the accused applicant has been cooperative during the course of investigation and since he was engaged in taking the legal recourse during the course of investigation and even after filing of the charge sheet, he could not be declared as proclaimed offender by the court concerned and no punitive process could be issued against him.
On the aforesaid ground, a prayer for anticipatory bail has been made.

6. Learned A.G.A. and learned counsel for the informant opposed the prayer for anticipatory bail and submitted that as a matter of fact, no marriage took place between the accused applicant and the prosecutrix of the case.
It is also submitted that the accused applicant made physical relation with the prosecutrix forcefully and by black-mailing her.

It is next submitted that although notarial marriage agreement was prepared but proper court marriage was never performed by the applicant with the prosecutrix and on false pretext of marriage and also by black-mailing and threatening her,
he physically exploited her
. It is next submitted that after further investigation, the concerned Magistrate court has opined that no offence under Section 498-A was found by the I.O. in the further investigation.

It is next submitted that the accused applicant is not cooperating with the trial Anurag Mishra vs State Of U.P. on 21 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/151251600/
2 court of the case and the cognizance was taken by the court.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
It is next submitted that non-bailable warrants have been issued against him and on the aforesaid grounds, a prayer for rejection of anticipatory bail application has been made.
7.

From the perusal of the record, prima facie, it appears that prosecutrix is a major lady and she willingly went with the accused applicant in a hotel and also to the house of aunt and lived with him and no obscene video has been procured by the I.O. during the course of investigation regarding to the prosecutrix.
It reveals from the perusal of the record that no process under Sections 82 & 83 Cr.P.C. has been issued against the applicant so far and he has not been declared as proclaimed offender by the court.
He has been cooperative during the course of investigation and now after filing of the charge sheet, no custodial interrogation is required and as such, he is entitled for anticipatory bail.

8. In Sushila Aggarwal and others vs. State (NCT of Delhi) and another, (2020) 5 SCC 1, the Hon'ble Apex Court has settled the controversy finally by holding the anticipatory bail need not be of limited duration invariably.

entities.text: Sushila Aggarwal and others vs. State (NCT of Delhi) and another, (2020) 5 SCC 1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In appropriate case, it can continue upto conclusion of trial.
It has been further held therein that anticipatory bail granted can, depending on the conduct and behavior of the accused, continue after filing of the charge sheet till end of trial.

It has been further held by the Hon'ble Apex Court that while considering an application for grant of anticipatory bail, the court has to consider the nature of the offence, the role of the person, the likelihood of his influencing the course of investigation, or tampering with evidence including intimidating witnesses, llikelihood of fleeing justice, such as leaving the country, etc.

It has further been held that Courts ought to be generally guided by considerations such as the nature and gravity of the offences, the role attributed to the applicant, and the facts of the case, while considering whether to grant anticipatory bail, or refuse it.
Whether to grant or not is a matter of discretion.

9. Hence, considering the settled principles of law regarding anticipatory bail, submissions of the learned counsel for the parties, nature of accusation, role of applicant and all attending facts and circumstances of the case, without expressing any opinion of the merits of the case, in my view, it is a fit case for anticipatory bail to the applicant till conclusion of trial in the matter.
10. The anticipatory bail application is allowed.

11. In the event of arrest of the applicant in the aforesaid case crime, he shall be released on anticipatory bail on his furnishing a personal bond of Rs. 50,000/- with two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the Court concerned with the following conditions :-
(i) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police officer or tamper with the evidence.

Anurag Mishra vs State Of U.P. on 21 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/151251600/

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: (ii) The applicant shall not pressurize/ intimidate the prosecution witness.
(iii) The applicant shall not commit an offence similar to the offence of which he is accused, or suspected, of the commission of which he is suspected.

(iv) The applicant shall not leave India without prior permission of the Court and if they have passport, the same shall be deposited by him before the S.S.P./S.P.
concerned.

12. In case of breach of any of the above conditions, the Investigating Officer shall be at liberty to file appropriate application for cancellation of anticipatory bail of the applicant in accordance with law.
